<!-- Source page: IRC -->

From <a href="wikipedia:Internet_Relay_Chat" class="wikilink" title="Wikipedia">Wikipedia</a>:

> Internet Relay Chat (IRC) is an <a href="wikipedia:Application_layer" class="wikilink" title="application layer">application layer</a> protocol that facilitates communication in the form of text. The chat process works on a <a href="wikipedia:Client%E2%80%93server_model" class="wikilink" title="client/server networking model">client/server networking model</a>.

## Clients

- <a href="irssi" class="wikilink" title="irssi">irssi</a>
- <a href="Quassel" class="wikilink" title="Quassel">Quassel</a>
- <a href="Weechat" class="wikilink" title="Weechat">Weechat</a> with the `irc` plugin

## Servers

- <a href="IRCd" class="wikilink" title="IRCd">IRCd</a> [^1][^2]

## Bouncers

An IRC bouncer stays connected to IRC servers so clients can disconnect without missing messages or losing the session.

- <a href="ZNC" class="wikilink" title="ZNC">ZNC</a>
- keep a client open in a <a href="tmux" class="wikilink" title="tmux">tmux</a> [^3][^4][^5] session

## Gateways

An IRC gateway recieves messages through other chat networks (e.g. <a href="wikipedia:XMPP" class="wikilink" title="|XMPP">|XMPP</a>) and forwards them through IRC.

- <a href="BitlBee" class="wikilink" title="BitlBee">BitlBee</a>
